raw_response:
I'm 76 this year, been farming these fields in Quzhou for 50 years. My wife and me, we're the only ones left on the farm now. Our children are working in the city, send some money back now and then, but I don't like to ask. Eight mu of land, that's what we have. Not much, but it's ours.

I do wheat and maize on six mu, double cropping like everyone in our village. The other two mu I keep for cotton — my father grew cotton, I grew cotton, it's what I know. Though at my age, bending down to pick cotton gets harder every year.

For the wheat, I'll plant around October 10th, same as I always do. I saved some seed from last year, but I mixed in some new seed from the shop because saved seed gets weaker after too many years. Last year we got about 800 jin per mu — not bad, not great. The year before was better. I'll put down base fertilizer before planting, about one bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu, then at jointing time in March if the wheat looks yellow I'll topdress with some urea. I usually irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water costs money now with the meters, so I don't waste it, but you can't skip it either.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, usually around June 12th. There's never enough time — sometimes we harvest wheat in the morning and plant maize in the afternoon. No time for deep plowing, just plant directly. For maize I use hybrid seed, buy it every year. Fertilizer all goes in at planting — maybe 20 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. I'll irrigate once if it doesn't rain, usually at the big trumpet leaf stage. Old Wang down the road tried no fertilizer one year because prices went up, and his maize was terrible. I'm not making that mistake.

For cotton, planted in late April. I put base fertilizer in the furrows, then topdress when it flowers. Need to spray for insects — the bollworm always comes. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll opening. Picking is the hard part. My wife and I do most of it slowly, but for the first pick I hire two women from the village to help for a couple of days. Costs money, but my back can't handle bending all day anymore.

Money is tight. Everything costs more now — fertilizer, seed, water, labor. I try to keep total spending around 4,000 yuan. You have to be careful. But I don't dare cut fertilizer too much — a bad harvest hurts more than saving a few hundred yuan. I learned that in the drought year... I think it was 2014. Terrible year. We lost almost half the wheat. Never again.
